name: MILLE BORNES
description: Racing card game for 2–6 players. Each hand is a race to 1000 km (or 700 km in 2–3 player with optional extension). Players play distance cards to advance; opponents play hazards (Accident, Out of Gas, Flat Tire, Stop, Speed Limit) which are countered by remedies and prevented by safeties. First to reach the target distance wins the hand. Game ends when one side reaches 5000 cumulative points.

content.text: Racing card game for 2–6 players. Each hand is a race to 1000 km (or 700 km in 2–3 player with optional extension). Players play distance cards to advance; opponents play hazards (Accident, Out of Gas, Flat Tire, Stop, Speed Limit) which are countered by remedies and prevented by safeties. First to reach the target distance wins the hand. Game ends when one side reaches 5000 cumulative points.

Created in 1954 by Edmond Dujardin in France as 1000 Bornes; derived from the American game Touring (1906, William Janson Roche). Name refers to the approximate length of Route Nationale 7 from Paris to the Italian border. Parker Brothers licensed and published it in the US from 1962; at one point it outsold Monopoly.
2, 3, 4, or 6 players. Four or six players form teams of two sharing a tableau.
Dedicated Mille Bornes deck of 106 cards: 18 hazards, 38 remedies, 4 safeties, 46 distance cards (25, 50, 75, 100, 200 km).

Shuffle and deal six cards to each player. Remainder forms the draw pile; a discard pile forms next to it. Each turn: draw one card from stock, then play one card to tableau or discard one. Hand size stays at six after play.

items.text: Extension (2–3 player): In 2- or 3-player play the target is 700 km. The first player to reach 700 km may either claim victory and end the hand, or call for an Extension that raises the target to 1000 km. First to 1000 km then wins the hand and scores a 200-point Extension bonus.
